title: Unregister and doctor legacy-record wording, scope and tests (WCLI-125 opus follow-up)
description: Follow-up from the opus APPROVE at 9ee8b83 of ward-cli#254 (WCLI-125), findings N1 to N6 and the item-7 stale comments. Each fails closed. N1: the unregister prompt (terminal-consent.ts second question) and result text (unregister.ts) say kept legacy approvals go live on re-registering; they cannot, since a re-registration gets a fresh nonce. N2: unregister removes another project's legacy binding at the same (root, device, inode) without naming it (legacyBindingsAt does not filter on projectId); show it or scope by projectId, with a test. N3: the in-transaction re-check can remove a current binding the user was never shown; refuse or re-prompt if the set changed, and approvalsRemoved must match what was removed. N4: the doctor's legacy remedy (reporting.ts) can be impossible and sits under 'inert and unreachable'; say 'register and approve again' or order it after the binding and manifest arms. N5: tests that cannot go red: the NUL pointer and .git-link guards need separating, the e2e re-clone approval assertions need fixing, and the approve-side legacy test must vary projectId, root and device. Item 7: stale comments at vault-state.ts near 1166-1169 and 84-88 and unregister.ts 4-8. N6: ADR 0026's Status line omits (a7), and the (a7) attribution of the APFS limit in the Consequences must be checked against opum-doc's record, read by ref. Open residual, decided and left: ADR 0005 carries no banner while review.toml includes its decision section.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Unregister's second question and result text no longer say kept legacy approvals go live on re-registering

Unregister names or scopes by projectId every binding it removes, a test covers a legacy binding of another project, and the in-transaction re-check refuses or re-prompts when the removal set changed, with approvalsRemoved matching what was removed
The doctor's legacy remedy says register and approve again, or is ordered after the binding and manifest arms, and a test covers it
Each of the NUL-pointer, .git-link, e2e re-clone and approve-side legacy tests fails when its own guard is removed
The stale comments in vault-state.ts and unregister.ts name the nonce, and ADR 0026's Status line and (a7) attribution agree with opum-doc's record read by ref

implementationNotes: Built on fix/wcli-137-legacy-record-wording. N1: the unregister second question, result text, header comment and ADR 0022 now say re-registering the same clone revives approvals this version wrote and never an earlier version approval (test: the prompt text, and the kept-approvals report). N2 and N3: unregister computes one removal set (removalSet in unregister.ts): the matched binding plus legacy bindings of the SAME project at this directory and the approvals belonging to them; a legacy binding of another project is neither shown, counted nor removed (test: another-project legacy binding and approval stay). The in-transaction check compares a fingerprint of every record removed and refuses with project_not_registered (the code a vanished binding already raised) if the set changed, and approvalsRemoved is the count actually removed (test: a binding appearing between the question and the write removes nothing). N4: the doctor legacy remedy now says register and approve again (ward init, then ward profile approve), if the profile is still declared; ordering after the binding arm is impossible because a legacy record never matches a binding, so the wording carries it. N5: the approve-side legacy test now varies projectId, root and device each alone; a CR-in-directory-name pointer case isolates the control-character guard; the e2e re-clone asserts a positive control for the old clone and that the old directory identity with the new nonce inherits no approval (red if the nonce is ignored whatever the inode); the NUL and .git-link cases are stated as outcome tests because realpath and the lstat file check double-guard them and cannot be isolated. Item 7: stale comments fixed in vault-state.ts and unregister.ts. N6: ADR 0026 Status now names (a7), and the APFS attribution was checked against DEC-255 (a7)(5), read by ref from opum-doc origin/dev: it matches. ADR 0026 notes unregister is project-scoped, which narrows (a7)(2)-(4) text, a legacy binding at the same tuple, to the one project shown; the narrowing is the finding N2 remedy and removes nothing beyond what (a7) allows. Mutation controls, each red: dropping the fingerprint comparison, the project filter, the isReplacedBy projectId comparison, the pointer control-character guard. bun run check 1201 pass, lore check, lore validate --strict, check-lore-agent-sources clean.

ROUND 2 (opus REQUEST CHANGES at b60ba1c; supersedes the N4 note above that said ordering after the binding arm was impossible and the wording carries it). The legacy stale-approval arm is now judged against the checkout as it stands: the binding is looked up under the nonce the checkout holds now. Registered (binding found, same project, profile declared): clearable, reapprove_required, remedy from , run ward profile approve

, which replaces the legacy record. Not registered, whether the checkout holds no nonce (M1/M2: pruned linked-worktree gitdir, invalid checkout-id file) or holds one whose binding was removed by a deliberate unregister (M1): clearable false, the check passes with code inert, and the record carries legacy: true, a discriminant the report words the hint from (register and approve again (ward init, then ward profile approve

), noting registering gives that checkout access); the frame is not inert and unreachable and nothing is asked of the user. Registered to another project, missing manifest and undeclared profile stay inert on their ordinary reasons. L-b (an inode-reuse re-clone attributed to the old record) goes away: a legacy record at a re-clone is the unregistered case, inert. Tests: no nonce, nonce left behind after unregister, pruned gitdir, invalid checkout-id, binding of another project, registered, and undeclared profile; the four unregistered cases each fail against b60ba1c reporting.ts. The reporting.ts Q2 header comment and ADR 0026 Consequences are corrected. L3 (a binding_changed code for the changed-set refusal) is filed separately for an opum-doc A/B.

== Fingerprint (the adversarial questions) ==
- Is the fingerprint sufficient? Every binding in `removing` shares the shown projectId and the checkout's (root, device, inode). findBinding requires the tuple through sameCheckout, and the legacy bindings are filtered on the tuple plus the project. So bindings are fully fingerprinted, and an owned approval is identified by (profile, checkoutId), with approvedAt to tell replacements apart. A changed identity set cannot collide: JSON.stringify of string arrays is unambiguous, and the comparison is order-sensitive, which can only cause false refusals.
- What is not fingerprinted? expiresAt and snapshot. A re-approval of the same profile on the same clone in the same millisecond would match. That is harmless: the consent is a count, and the slot is the same approval.
- Does a refusal leave the vault untouched? Yes. The throw is inside the bun:sqlite transaction (sqlite-vault-store.ts:537), and the race test asserts bindings and approvals unchanged.
- The fingerprint also refuses when approvals changed after the user declined removing them. That fails closed, and it is defensible because the count shown changed.

== New findings, ranked (none blocks) ==
L1 LOW (lead item, since the AC's test clause is at stake). N4 is half fixed, and the "cannot be ordered" reason does not hold.
- reporting.ts:486-488 renders every clearable:false entry as "inert and unreachable — <remedy>". The new legacy remedy therefore prints under exactly the frame N4 objected to.
- The check code stays "inert", and reporting.test.ts:1096-1099 pins that for the legacy arm too.
- The new comment at reporting.ts:424-427 ("It is not an 'inert and unreachable' record") contradicts both the output and the test.
- Why the reason fails: probed.checkoutId is already in hand (compared at :434). The arm could call findBinding with the record's tuple plus probed.checkoutId and the manifest probe. That would let it say "approve again" when the checkout is registered, "register, then approve" when it is not, and "inert" when the profile is undeclared.
- Test gap: the legacy row (reporting.test.ts:957-959) asserts only "a legacy approval, …; it authorises nothing". A full revert goes red, because the old text lacks that preamble. A revert of only the remedy clause back to the old, possibly impossible "approve the profile again from that checkout" stays green. AC index 2's "a test covers it" holds for the preamble, not for the remedy N4 was about.
- Fix: assert "register and approve again (ward init", and either make the rendering frame-aware or order the arm on the probed binding.

L2 LOW (latent). withoutBinding is not project-scoped (unregister.ts:74-80).
- It drops every localBinding matching root, device, inode and checkoutId, whatever the project.
- Scenario: a P-legacy and a Q-legacy binding exist at one tuple, and the user unregisters P. removalSet correctly excludes Q and shows only P, but withoutBinding(P-legacy) also deletes Q-legacy, because both have checkoutId undefined. Q's binding goes unshown and uncounted. Q's legacy approvals stay, now orphaned: legacyBindingsAt finds no Q binding to anchor a later unregister.
- This contradicts AC1's "scopes by projectId every binding it removes" and the implementation note's "neither shown, counted nor removed".
- Reachability: current flows cannot create two bindings at one tuple, because of binding_conflict at project.ts:161 and :169. Whether 0.1.1 could is unverified (see below), so this needs a merged or hand-edited vault at minimum.
- Fix: add `entry.projectId !== binding.projectId ||` to the localBindings filter. Pin it with a unit test seeding P-legacy and Q-legacy at one tuple and asserting Q-legacy survives.

L3 LOW. The refusal code misreports.
- On a changed set, unregister throws project_not_registered. Its message, "This checkout is not registered with Ward…", and its hint, "Run `ward init`…" (errors.ts:252-256), are both false in the race this check now detects: the checkout is still registered, and ward init answers already-registered.
- The catalog already has the right pattern: secret_changed (errors.ts:310) and profile_changed (:411), type "conflict", "…changed while this command was running…; run the command again".
- Fix: a binding_changed code of that shape (a catalog addition), or at least keep project_not_registered only for present === undefined.
- It fails closed. Reusing the code for the projectId-changed case predates this PR; the fingerprint arm widens it.

NIT-1. The re-clone positive-control comment (project-binding.test.ts:453-455) says `after` has "the old directory identity". It has the re-clone's inode, which is the old one only if the inode was reused. The assertion at :464-471 is still trivially undefined, because after.checkoutId is undefined. It is harmless now that :486-493 carries the proof, but the comment overstates.

NIT-2. The CR test isolates only the `\r` arm of /[\r\n\0]/ (checkout.ts:113). A mid-line `\n` in a directory name, as in "gitdir: <dir-with-LF>\n", is also isolable the same way and is not covered. The writer's "isolates the control-character guard" is true of `\r` only.

Pre-existing, non-blocking: withoutBinding never touches staleProfileApprovals. A yes to both questions leaves a removed binding's stale-version approvals in place. This is not from this diff.

No new leak: the unregister output and data are unchanged apart from wording (projectId only). The doctor's legacy remedy interpolates record.root and record.profile. Both were already in the entry (`checkout`, `profile`) and in the clearable remedy, and the text path passes through escapeForDisplay at :485-488. No nonce reaches any output.

== If opum-doc rules the other way (remove every project's legacy records at the tuple, and list each) ==
Code:
- removalSet drops the projectId filter (unregister.ts:101), so `removing` is the matched binding plus all legacy bindings, and `owned` covers every project's.
- UnregisterQuestion (approvals.ts) gains a per-project list of {projectId, approvals}. unregisterPrompt (terminal-consent.ts) renders each project through escapeForDisplay.
- Decide whether the first question's count is per-project or a total.
- The result data gains a per-project removed list. The "Checkout unregistered" text and the kept-approvals text name every project. The declined text says all were kept.
- The fingerprint already covers projectId, so the in-transaction compare stays. The `present.binding.projectId` check stays.
- withoutBinding's tuple-only filter (L2) becomes correct by accident. Make it explicit rather than leaving it to chance.
Tests and docs:
- The N2 test inverts: Q's legacy binding and approval are removed, named in both questions and in the output, and approvalsRemoved counts both projects.
- The "drop the project filter" mutation control disappears. Add a test that the prompt lists every project, and one that the escape holds.
- ADR 0026 Consequences (and the ADR 0022 note) revert to the tuple wording, adding "each project listed".
- No external JSON schema references approvalsRemoved (grep), so the contract change is the envelope data alone.
